CONS: Less control; tabs will unfreeze immediately when clicked, and icons won't show the frozen state.

html_options_suspend_screen_capturing_to.message: On a suspended tab, the extension can display an image preview of the what the tab
looked like just before it was suspended.
The screen capturing feature is experimental and can cause significant CPU usage as
well as slightly increased memory usage.
If you notice strange behaviour such as tabs taking a long time to suspend, or chrome
crashing unexpectedly, try turning this feature off.

html_options_suspend_force_screen_captur.message: Enable high quality screen capture mode
When disabled, screen captures have the following limitations to aid in performance:
- Will not capture screen if it takes more than 1 minute to generate image
- Maximum height of screen capture limited to 5000px
Enabling high quality screen capture mode may significantly increase CPU load

html_monitor_intro.message: Tab memory is approximate. A threefold difference in either direction is possible; this is not a guaranteed error bound.

html_monitor_more.message: How the estimate works and why numbers differ

html_monitor_method_detail.message: The monitor uses JS heap, DOM, images, canvas, media and page resources with approximate coefficients. Some memory is shared with other tabs or inaccessible to extensions. The number does not guarantee how much RAM closing the tab will release. Without the processes API, CPU represents main-thread long-task activity, not total processor usage.

html_monitor_chrome_detail.message: Chrome’s hover card also shows a memory estimate attributed to the page (private footprint), not guaranteed RAM savings. Shared processes, sampling time and different metrics cause discrepancies. The Chrome memory column uses the processes API: shared processes are split equally between associated tabs. It does not read the hover card directly. The API is available in Dev/Canary, not Stable or regular Beta.

html_monitor_states_detail.message: Extension placeholder: a fixed estimate of ≈4 MB, not a measurement. Discard with the original URL: the last saved value for that URL is marked “before discard”; no history means a dash. Historical values are excluded from the current total. Discard unloads page contents; freeze pauses execution while retaining them in memory. Keeping the URL does not itself mean the tab still occupies hundreds of megabytes.
